set.prevailing_wage_basis: RFP No. 26-004A (May 1, 2026), pages 11 to 12: pro formas must assume State prevailing wages and/or Federal Davis-Bacon wages and compliance with the City CWA; HOME and HOME-ARP Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more assisted units (24 CFR 92.354, restated in RFP Exhibit IV page 31). Santa Ana Community Workforce Agreement with the Los Angeles/Orange Counties Building and Construction Trades Council, effective June 6, 2023 (reproduced as Exhibit V of RFP 26-004A, pages 54 to 78): Section 2.2.4 makes 'any Affordable Housing projects that receive City funds' covered Project Work, with no dollar threshold (the $750,000 multi-trade and $100,000 specialty thresholds in 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 apply to public works contracts); Section 5.1 requires covered employees to be paid the hourly rates in the applicable prevailing wage determination; Section 11.2 requires compliance with state prevailing wage law and Santa Ana Municipal Code 33-206. RFP 26-004A Section IV (page 24) and General Terms item (2) (page 19) state the CWA applies to City-funded affordable housing projects, is enforced in the final City agreement, requires union hiring hall referral, and requires at least 30% of craft hours by Santa Ana (Tier 1) or Orange County (Tier 2) ZIP code residents, veterans or MC3 pre-apprenticeship graduates, measured on certified payroll; each proposer signs Attachment H and each contractor signs a Letter of Assent. SAMC 33-206 (emergency ordinance, December 16, 2014) applies state prevailing wage law to City public works as defined in Labor Code 1720, so it adds no coverage beyond state law; the local layer is the CWA. Note: the RFP's Exhibit II sample pre-loan commitment (page 44) leaves the Labor Code 1720 state prevailing wage determination to the developer, but the CWA wage clause applies to all City-funded affordable housing regardless.
set.layering_notes: Santa Ana is the deepest city pool in Orange County: about $17,500,000 in one RFP, mostly HOME, with loans at 3% simple interest, 55-year term, repaid from 50% of residual receipts, TCAC developer fee limits and a Review Panel scoring process under the 2020 Affordable Housing Funds Policies and Procedures (opened). Any City-funded affordable housing project is covered by the June 6, 2023 Community Workforce Agreement (Section 2.2.4, no dollar threshold): contractors sign a Letter of Assent, hire through union hiring halls and pay prevailing wage rates, and the project must reach 30% of craft hours from Santa Ana and Orange County ZIP codes, veterans or MC3 graduates; budget a labor premium even for small or ownership projects that might otherwise be exempt under Labor Code 1720(c). Davis-Bacon applies to HOME projects of 12 or more assisted units. Stack with County 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA loans and OCHA or SAHA PBVs, OCHFT gap loans (WISEPlace took $2,500,000 OCHFT MHSA plus $1,500,000 County ARPA) and 4% or 9% credits. The County NOFA pays $95,000 to $105,000 per unit inside Santa Ana, so the City loan is normally the larger local layer. RFP PDF, RFP page, policies PDF and FY 2025-26 Q4 quarterly report opened on santa-ana.gov and its Google Cloud document store.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: Housing Successor funds are offered through RFP 26-004A ($2,630,914), and the RFP states the City CWA applies to City-funded affordable housing projects and is enforced in the final agreement. Santa Ana Community Workforce Agreement with the Los Angeles/Orange Counties Building and Construction Trades Council, effective June 6, 2023 (reproduced as Exhibit V of RFP 26-004A, pages 54 to 78): Section 2.2.4 makes 'any Affordable Housing projects that receive City funds' covered Project Work, with no dollar threshold (the $750,000 multi-trade and $100,000 specialty thresholds in 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 apply to public works contracts); Section 5.1 requires covered employees to be paid the hourly rates in the applicable prevailing wage determination; Section 11.2 requires compliance with state prevailing wage law and Santa Ana Municipal Code 33-206. RFP 26-004A Section IV (page 24) and General Terms item (2) (page 19) state the CWA applies to City-funded affordable housing projects, is enforced in the final City agreement, requires union hiring hall referral, and requires at least 30% of craft hours by Santa Ana (Tier 1) or Orange County (Tier 2) ZIP code residents, veterans or MC3 pre-apprenticeship graduates, measured on certified payroll; each proposer signs Attachment H and each contractor signs a Letter of Assent. SAMC 33-206 (emergency ordinance, December 16, 2014) applies state prevailing wage law to City public works as defined in Labor Code 1720, so it adds no coverage beyond state law; the local layer is the CWA. State law alone would be uncertain: Labor Code 1720(c)(4) excludes housing paid solely from former redevelopment Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund moneys, 1720(c)(5)(E) exempts qualifying below-market residential loans, and 1720(c)(3) exempts de minimis subsidy (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720). The trigger rests on the CWA wage clause, not on Labor Code 1720. Caveat: the CWA says 'City funds'; the RFP treats Housing Successor funds as covered, but a Housing Authority land disposition outside the RFP was not tested.
set.layering_notes: Small compared with the County's $29,000,000 LMIHAF but flexible: no federal strings, can serve moderate income and mixed-use, and the Housing Authority's land is the real asset (Crossroads and FX Residences were built on 65- and 99-year ground leases). Pair with HOME in the same RFP, SAHA PBVs, County MHSA/BHSA capital and OCHFT. Projects funded through the City RFP are covered by the June 6, 2023 Community Workforce Agreement (union hiring halls, prevailing wage rates, 30% local craft hours), so budget a labor premium even where a Labor Code 1720(c) exemption would otherwise apply. FY 2024-25 Housing Successor Annual Report PDF and the Successor Agency page opened on santa-ana.gov; CWA text read in RFP 26-004A Exhibit V.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: HOME: 24 CFR 92.354 Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more HOME-assisted units (restated in RFP 26-004A Exhibit IV page 31, also for HOME-ARP); CDBG: Davis-Bacon applies to residential construction of 8 or more units (HCD Act of 1974 Section 110). Local layer: HOME development loans are awarded through RFP 26-004A, and the City CWA (effective June 6, 2023, RFP Exhibit V) Section 2.2.4 covers any affordable housing project receiving City funds, Section 5.1 requires prevailing wage rates, and RFP Section IV (page 24) requires union hiring hall referral and 30% local craft hours (Santa Ana and Orange County ZIP codes, veterans or MC3 graduates). SAMC 33-206 (2014) only adopts state prevailing wage law for City public works.

set.typical_award_size: $200,000 per unit for category one (condos, townhomes, multifamily units and conversions of non-residential or non-code-compliant space; single-family homes are not eligible), $125,000 per ADU and $50,000 per SRO unit, paid at completion once the 55-year workforce Use Deed Restriction is recorded. Funding: $1,000,000 inaugural NOFA LP-001 (released April 16, 2025; 8 applications) reserved $725,000 for two Kings Beach projects (Steelhead Avenue Cottage Court, 3 tiny homes, $600,000; accessible ADU, $125,000). NOFA LP-002, posted February 6, 2026, offered $3,275,000 ($3,000,000 of new TOT approved February 3, 2026 plus $275,000 carryover), drew 12 applications (55 units, $10,550,000 requested) and reserved $3,250,000 for four projects: Lake Forest Multifamily (12 studios, Tahoe City, $2,400,000), Dollar Hill Tiny Homes (3 units, $600,000) and two tiny home ADUs in Lake Forest and Cedar Flat ($125,000 each).
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 10, 2026. The February 2026 NOFA LP-002 (applications February 25 to March 18, 2026) is fully reserved. The May 11, 2026 Board memo says staff will bring revised guidelines to the Board later in 2026, and the County opened a community survey in August 2026; a future NOFA depends on new TOT funding recommended through the NTCA TOT-TBID Dollars at Work program.
set.cycle_notes: NOFA rounds when TOT funding is approved (LP-001 April 2025, LP-002 February 2026); 3-week application windows; randomized lottery prioritizing categories one and two when oversubscribed (used in 2026); projects have 2 years from the award letter to complete. Guidelines under revision after the August 2026 survey. The LP-001 and LP-002 NOFA PDFs are no longer posted (DocumentCenter links return 404); the program page and Guidelines remain the current sources.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific rule. The Launchpad Guidelines (April 2025, Section III) require compliance with all applicable federal, state and local laws but do not mention prevailing wage; the program page, Reserved Projects page and May 11, 2026 Board memo also say nothing on it; the LP-002 NOFA PDF is no longer posted. Only the general Labor Code 1720 framework applies (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): the TOT grant paid at completion is public funds under 1720(b)(1) and is not a loan, so 1720(c)(5)(E) does not apply, but 1720(c)(1) excludes private residential projects on private property not built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency or local public housing authority, and 1720(c)(3) excludes de minimis subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost. Most Launchpad awards (ADUs at $125,000, tiny home projects at $600,000) sit at or near these thresholds; a larger award such as Lake Forest Multifamily ($2,400,000) would need a project-specific determination.
set.layering_notes: placer.ca.gov sits behind Cloudflare; the same County pages and DocumentCenter files open on the placerair.org host, and Board memos are on content.govdelivery.com/attachments/CAPLACER. Launchpad is a per-unit grant rather than a loan and is sized for small infill projects in Kings Beach, Tahoe City and the North Shore; a 10-unit workforce project could draw $2 million, which is meaningful against TRPA coverage and construction costs in the Basin. It pays only at completion, so it is bridge-financed. Guidelines Section III.f bars combining Launchpad with any other County program or subsidy unless the Board approves. The workforce (not income) restriction means it does not fit LIHTC deals directly but can fund unrestricted middle-income units in a mixed-income project. North Lake Tahoe TOT also funds the Workforce Housing Preservation Program and the Dollar Creek Crossing effort.
